newsitem.title: CANADA: Cambior cites higher production for gains.
newsitem.headline: Cambior cites higher production for gains.

text.p: Cambior Inc on Thursday credited rising production at its Omai gold mine in Guyana and the Doyon mine in Quebec for its third-quarter profit.
Cambior earlier today reported third-quarter earnings of US$3.3 million or US$O.05 a share, versus a year earlier loss of US$4.7 million or US$0.09 a share.
Third-quarter revenues were a record US$91.7 million, up from US$64.2 million in last year's third quarter.
The company credited revived production at the Omai mine, which accounted for last year's third-quarter loss.
Omai produced 77,000 ounces of gold in the third quarter, up from the 58,000 produced in the second quarter.
The company said it expanded capacity at the mine through a mill expansion in July. The mill operated at full capacity in August for an average throughput of 18,300 tonnes a day for the quarter.
The fourth quarter should benefit from a full quarter of operation at the expanded facility, Cambior said.
In August 1995, Cambior shut down the Omai mine after a tailings dam failed.
At the Doyon mine, production rose 30 percent to 27,000 ounces of gold from the second quarter, Cambior said.

"We expect to meet our production targets for the year 1996 and will establish, during the second half of the year, an improved and sustainable level of production and financial performance," president Louis Gignac said in a statement.
Cambior said it spent US$6.8 million on exploration in the first nine months of the year and decided to accelerate its exploration budget in Peru and Mexico.
Cambior's board approved a semi-annual dividend of US$0.052 a common share payable on December 20, 1996 to shareholders of record on November 22, 1996.
